meta.title: Lba Cra And Council Formal Meeting

votes.description: The Local Building Authority Board approved the minutes from its April 15, 2025 meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the LBA Capital Projects Fund Budget for FY 2025-26 and refer to a new public hearing on June 3, 2025
votes.description: The LBA Board closed the first public hearing on the proposed budget for the Capital Projects Fund (covering bond debt service for Glendale and Marmalade Libraries) and referred the item to a second public hearing on June 3, 2025.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the LBA and convene as the CRA
votes.description: The Board adjourned the Local Building Authority meeting and reconvened as the Community Reinvestment Agency Board.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the CRA Budget for FY 2025-26 and refer to a new public hearing on June 3, 2025
votes.description: The CRA Board closed the first public hearing on the proposed Community Reinvestment Agency budget for FY 2025-26 and referred the item to a second public hearing on June 3, 2025.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the CRA Board and convene as the Salt Lake City Council
votes.description: The Board adjourned the Community Reinvestment Agency meeting and reconvened as the Salt Lake City Council.

votes.motion: Approve April 1, 2025 formal Council meeting minutes
votes.description: The City Council approved the minutes from its April 1, 2025 formal meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 13 of 2025, Celebrating June 2025 as Pride Month
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall recognizing June 2025 as Pride Month in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Items G1 through G4 (grant applications) to a future Consent Agenda for action
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on four grant applications (UOVC Victim Advocates, Bonneville Shoreline Trailhead Land Purchase, School Age Quality Grant, and DWS Teen Afterschool Prevention Grant) and referred them to a future consent agenda.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 29 of 2025, amending the FY 2025 final budget of the Salt Lake City Library including the employment staffing document
votes.description: The Council adopted the Library Budget Amendment No. 2 for FY 2024-25, which includes required annual true-ups of property tax increments for the Utah Inland Port Authority, Convention Center Hotel, and the CRA.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer items G5-G20 to a new public hearing on June 3, 2025
votes.description: The Council closed the first public hearing on the FY 2025-26 Mayor's Recommended Budget items (city budget, library budget, tax levy, fee schedule, compensation, labor MOUs, code amendments, CIP, and UTA interlocal addendum) and referred them to a second public hearing on June 3, 2025.

votes.motion: Not adopt item I2 (public art peacemaking projects line item) and include a Legislative Intent to allocate $14,000 ($2,000 per district) from fund balance to the Community and Neighborhoods budget for FY26 for an Arts Council public arts program for small district-based peacemaking projects, with an administrative report due by December 2025
votes.description: As part of Budget Amendment No. 5 for FY 2024-25, the Council declined a specific budget item and instead added a Legislative Intent directing the creation of a public arts peacemaking program with equitable, transparent, and council-member-inclusive criteria.

votes.motion: Not adopt item I3, close Budget Amendment No. 5, and add more specifications with the Legislative Intent as clarified in the previous motion for item I2
votes.description: The Council declined another budget sub-item, formally closed Budget Amendment No. 5 for FY 2024-25, and incorporated additional specifications into the previously adopted Legislative Intent regarding public arts peacemaking projects.

The Council approved the consent agenda, which included setting a public hearing date for an alley closure at Madsen Park and approving four board appointments (Planning Commission: Lilah Rosenfield, Michael Vela, Jeffrey Barrett; Bicycle Advisory Committee: Esther Daranciang).
